nonblocking_findings: NB-1: leaderboards.schoolId in the Drizzle schema (packages/db/src/schema/primary.ts:229) is still typed nullable even though migration 0026 sets it to NOT NULL at the DB level. TenantDB injects schoolId on FLAT inserts so this is not a runtime issue, but the TypeScript type should be aligned with the migration in a follow-up (Review A NB-1).

NB-2: The PGlite test helper seedSchoolAndUser uses sql.raw with string-interpolated schoolId. The input is a hardcoded test constant, so this is not a runtime vulnerability, but future test helpers should use parameterized queries (Review B NB-1).

NB-3: The standalone apps/advantage-games rankingRoute.ts and completeRoute.ts remain force-static mocks without auth or tenant context. This is the intended Phase 4 boundary — host apps must call getSchoolLeaderboard/recordGameCompletion with a real TenantDB. Standalone app cannot be safely imported until Phase 5+ wiring (Review B NB-2).

NB-4: updateLessonProgress validates lessonId as a UUID but does not yet verify tenant ownership of the lesson. plan.md correctly defers this Tier 2 check as [b] deferred:infra (Review B NB-3, Decision 4.4).

NB-5: RankingDialog.tsx expects a difficulty-keyed Record (data?.[diff]) but rankingRoute.ts returns a flat array per leaderboardResponseSchema. With empty mock data this is invisible; must be resolved in Phase 5+ when real data flows (Review C NB-P4-001/NB-P4-004).
NB-6: DIFFICULTY_KEYS is exported from rankingRoute.ts but RankingDialog.tsx hardcodes its own difficulties array. Phase 5+ should import DIFFICULTY_KEYS to stay in sync (Review C NB-P4-002).
NB-7: 65 legacy 'normal' difficulty references remain across other games; Phase 5+ scope per Decision 4.3 (Review C NB-P4-003).

NB-8: useGameStore.ts Difficulty type still includes 'normal'. Per the strategy's changed-contract-risk note, the per-game Difficulty types migrate in Phase 5+.
